name: T58 IVB -- Initial Volatility Breakout (reconstructed, NQ 5m)
description: RECONSTRUCTED, not copied -- I never saw RoboQuant's source code, only a screen-recorded promo showing their optimizer's parameter names/values for a strategy called 'IVB -- Initial Volatility Breakout (NASDAQ)': Max Contraction Ratio (IB / avg IB range) 0.5, Trailing IB Range Lookback 10 trading days, Volume Surge Multiplier (vs RTH avg) 1.6, RTH Volume Lookback 5 bars, Stop Loss 3x ATR, Take Profit 2x ATR. This file re-implements that CONCEPT (a well-known 'initial balance / opening-range breakout, filtered to only trade days where the opening range was unusually narrow vs its own recent history, confirmed by a volume surge') using this app's own indicator primitives -- opening_range_high/low for the IB levels, relative_volume for the volume-surge filter, and a NEW ib_contraction_ratio operand (added to app/strategy/manual.py + app/strategy/indicators-adjacent session logic in this same delivery) for the contraction filter, since the app previously had no way to compare today's opening-range width to its own trailing multi-day average. ASSUMPTIONS I had to make that weren't visible on screen: (1) the IB window itself -- I used the first 15 minutes of RTH (09:30-09:45 ET), a common default for this style of system, but the video never showed the exact window length; (2) the ATR period backing the 3x/2x stop and target (14, this app's usual default) -- the video showed the multiples but not the underlying ATR period; (3) a session-close flatten IS included -- risk_management.time_based_exit fires at 15:55 ET, force-closing any open position before the 16:00 RTH close, so a breakout can't silently carry overnight gap risk the hypothesis makes no claim about. HAS NOT BEEN BACKTESTED against real NQ data as part of this delivery -- run it through Run & Report and then Full Pipeline before trusting any number from it, exactly like every other strategy in this library.
